shared_elements: upright freestanding stone monument on a museum plinth
shallow low-relief carving on a single stone face
rounded curvilinear motifs enclosed by raised outlines
eye-like paired ovals within a rounded frame
horizontal banded divisions across the surface
justification: Both are large upright stone blocks carved in shallow relief with rounded, outlined motifs including discs and paired eye-like ovals, and both are photographed on museum plinths, which supplies a generic likeness of medium and presentation. The decisive difference is compositional: A is a flat rectangular slab covered in a strict multi-row, multi-column grid of equal-sized cartouches, while B is an irregular boulder shaped into one large frontal anthropomorphic figure with headdress, torso and belt, with no repeating grid at all.
